correctness.rationale: Over any algebraically closed field, Bezout with the blown-up smooth conic implies (-K)·F>=deg(F) for any nonexceptional irreducible curve different from the conic. Adjunction then forces all negative irreducible curves to be exactly six exceptional (-1) curves, fifteen pair-lines (-1), and the unique (-2) conic, with the displayed integral intersection form. A negative definite support consists of mutually disjoint (-1) curves, with at most one exceptional curve if the (-2) conic is included (Schur complement -2+s). Pairwise intersecting edge families in a complete graph are stars or triangles, yielding the explicit generating function and coefficients. The primary chamber/support correspondence assures realization by big divisors. The independently executed verifier enumerated every 22-curve principal subset of at most six components using exact Bareiss determinants and the rank-six negativity bound; it reproduced every coefficient, total 1898 and conic subtotal 648. Larger supports cannot be negative definite by Hodge index.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete chamber-spectrum classification on the minimal resolution of the simplest singular degeneration of a smooth cubic. It gives an exact birational invariant governing big-divisor negative supports and piecewise volume behavior, refines it by support size and whether the distinguished contracted (-2)-root occurs, and proves position independence for all six distinct points on any smooth conic. It quantifies the nontrivial drop 2764 to 1898 from the smooth case. The calculation is not a random finite parameter slice, a simple table lookup or a renaming of the general Zariski-chamber algorithm; it provides the complete negative-curve proof and the star/triangle combinatorial mechanism.
